at vande.explanation: "At vande" means "to water" plants, flowers and lawns: Hun vander plænen om aftenen (She waters the lawn in the evening). It comes from vand (water).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vande** blomsterne, fordi det ikke har regnet.
sentence.en: I have to water the flowers because it has not rained.

at vare.explanation: "At vare" means "to last", about how long something goes on: Filmen varer to timer (The movie lasts two hours). Det varer ikke længe (It won't be long).

sentence.da: Mødet vil **vare** i cirka en time.
sentence.en: The meeting will last about an hour.

at vaske.explanation: "At vaske" means "to wash", for clothes, dishes, your hands or the car: Jeg vasker bilen (I wash the car). To wash yourself, say vaske sig (to wash oneself). At vaske op means "to do the dishes".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vaske** tøjet i dag.
sentence.en: I want to wash the clothes today.

at vaske gulv.explanation: "At vaske gulv" means "to mop the floor" and is said without gulvet (the floor): Vi vasker gulv om lørdagen (We mop the floor on Saturdays). For one spill, use at tørre op (to wipe up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske gulv**, fordi det er meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to mop the floor because it is very dirty.

at vaske op.explanation: "At vaske op" means "to do the dishes" by hand: Hvem vasker op i dag? (Who is doing the dishes today?). Do not mix it up with at vaske (to wash), which is used for clothes, hands or the car.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske op** efter maden.
sentence.en: I have to do the dishes after the meal.

at vaske sig.explanation: "At vaske sig" means "to wash yourself". The little word sig (oneself) becomes mig (myself) when you talk about yourself: jeg vasker mig (I wash myself). If you wash something else, you drop it: at vaske hænder (to wash hands) or at vaske tøj (to wash clothes).

sentence.da: Han skal **vaske sig** før maden.
sentence.en: He has to wash himself before the meal.

at vaske tøj.explanation: "At vaske tøj" means "to do laundry", literally to wash clothes: Min søster vasker tøj hver søndag (My sister does laundry every Sunday). For dishes, say at vaske op (to wash the dishes).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske tøj**, fordi jeg ikke har flere rene sokker.
sentence.en: I have to do laundry because I have no more clean socks.

at veje.explanation: "At veje" means "to weigh". You can weigh something (Jeg vejer pakken, I weigh the package) or have a certain weight (Jeg vejer 70 kilo, I weigh 70 kilos).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **veje** pakken i dag.
sentence.en: I want to weigh the package today.

at vende.explanation: "At vende" means "to turn" something over or around: Jeg vender kortet (I turn the card over). For turning in a direction, say at dreje (to turn): Drej til venstre (Turn left).

sentence.da: Du kan **vende** bladet og læse videre.
sentence.en: You can turn the page and read on.

at vende sig.explanation: "At vende sig" means "to turn around" with your own body: Han vendte sig og smilede (He turned around and smiled). Do not mix it up with at vænne sig til (to get used to).

sentence.da: Han vil **vende sig** og se på mig.
sentence.en: He wants to turn around and look at me.

at vende tilbage.explanation: "At vende tilbage" means "to return", to come back to a place or a topic: Han vender tilbage til byen (He returns to the city). It is also a polite way to say you will answer later: Jeg vender tilbage til dig (I will get back to you).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vende tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: We want to return to Denmark next year.

at vente.explanation: "At vente" means "to wait": Jeg venter på bussen (I am waiting for the bus). Vent lidt means "Wait a moment". It can also mean "to expect": Hun venter barn (She is expecting a baby).

sentence.da: Vi må **vente** lidt her.
sentence.en: We have to wait a little here.

at vente på.explanation: "At vente på" means "to wait for" someone or something: Jeg venter på dig (I am waiting for you). The little word på (on) always stays with it. Vent! means "Wait!".

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vente på** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to wait for the bus.

at vide.explanation: "At vide" means "to know" a fact: Jeg ved det ikke (I do not know). For knowing a person or a place, Danish uses a different word, at kende (to know someone).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **vide** mere.
sentence.en: I would like to know more.

at ville.explanation: "At ville" means "to want to": Jeg vil have en kop kaffe (I want a cup of coffee). Adding gerne (gladly) makes it polite: Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe (I would like a cup of coffee). Vil is about wanting, not just will: for a duty, use skal (have to): Jeg skal gå (I have to go).

sentence.da: Du skal **ville** lære dansk.
sentence.en: You have to want to learn Danish.

at vinde.explanation: "At vinde" means "to win": Hun vinder løbet (She wins the race). You can also win a prize: at vinde en præmie (to win a prize).

sentence.da: Vi kan **vinde** kampen i dag.
sentence.en: We can win the match today.

at vinke.explanation: "At vinke" means "to wave" your hand: Hun vinker til mig (She waves at me). Use til (to) for who you wave at, and add farvel (goodbye) to wave goodbye: Han vinkede farvel (He waved goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vinke** til dig, når toget kører.
sentence.en: I will wave to you when the train leaves.

at virke.explanation: "At virke" means "to work", for things that function, and also "to seem": Bilen virker ikke (The car does not work). Han virker træt (He seems tired).

sentence.da: Telefonen vil ikke **virke** i dag.
sentence.en: The phone won't work today.

at vise.explanation: "At vise" means "to show": Jeg viser billedet (I show the picture). When you show someone something, the person comes first, with no word for "to" in front: Hun viser mig bogen (She shows me the book). Vis mig means "Show me".

sentence.da: Kan du **vise** mig vej?
sentence.en: Can you show me the way?

at vise sig.explanation: "At vise sig" means "to turn out", when you find out how something really is: Det viste sig, at bilen var gratis (It turned out that the car was free). Hun viste sig at være meget flink (She turned out to be very nice).

sentence.da: Det kan **vise sig**, at han har ret.
sentence.en: It may turn out that he is right.

at vokse.explanation: "At vokse" means "to grow", for children, plants and things: Børn vokser hurtigt (Children grow fast). To grow up is at vokse op: Jeg voksede op i Odense (I grew up in Odense). To grow tomatoes, use at dyrke (to cultivate).

sentence.da: Planterne kan **vokse** meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: The plants can grow very fast.

at vokse op.explanation: "At vokse op" means "to grow up", to spend your childhood somewhere: Jeg voksede op i Jylland (I grew up in Jutland). Without op, at vokse means "to grow", for example plants: Træet vokser hurtigt (The tree grows quickly).

sentence.da: Mine børn skal **vokse op** på landet.
sentence.en: My children will grow up in the countryside.

at vågne.explanation: "At vågne" means "to wake up" by yourself: Jeg vågner klokken syv (I wake up at seven). When someone else wakes you, Danish uses at vække (to wake someone).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vågne** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I have to wake up at seven.

at vågne op.explanation: "At vågne op" means "to wake up", the moment you become awake. People often just say at vågne (to wake up), so the op (up) is optional. Do not mix it up with at stå op (to get out of bed).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vågne op** tidligt i morgen.
sentence.en: I want to wake up early tomorrow.

at vække.explanation: "At vække" means "to wake someone": Jeg vækker børnene klokken syv (I wake the kids at seven). To wake up yourself, say at vågne (to wake up): Jeg vågnede tidligt (I woke up early).

sentence.da: Kan du **vække** mig klokken seks?
sentence.en: Can you wake me at six?

at vælge.explanation: "At vælge" means "to choose" or "to pick": Jeg vælger den røde (I choose the red one). Et valg means both "a choice" and "an election".

sentence.da: Du må **vælge** rød eller blå.
sentence.en: You may choose red or blue.

at vælte.explanation: "At vælte" means "to knock over" and "to tip over": Jeg vælter koppen (I knock over the cup). Something can also go over by itself: Træet væltede (The tree fell over).

forms.en: I have knocked over / tipped over

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **vælte** glasset!
sentence.en: Be careful, you might knock over the glass!

at vænne sig til.explanation: "At vænne sig til" means "to get used to": Jeg vænner mig til kulden (I am getting used to the cold). Once it is done, say vant til: Jeg er vant til kulden (I am used to the cold).

sentence.da: Det tager tid at **vænne sig til** et nyt sted.
sentence.en: It takes time to get used to a new place.

at være.explanation: "At være" means "to be": Jeg er glad (I am happy), Hun er i Danmark (She is in Denmark), Det er en bog (It is a book). The present form er is the same for everyone: jeg er (I am), han er (he is), vi er (we are).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **være** hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: I want to be at home today.

at være bange for.explanation: "At være bange for" means "to be afraid of": Jeg er bange for edderkopper (I am afraid of spiders). Before a verb, add at: Jeg er bange for at falde (I am afraid of falling).

sentence.da: Børn kan **være bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: Children can be afraid of the dark.

at være enig.explanation: "At være enig" means "to agree" and literally says "to be agreed": Jeg er enig med dig (I agree with you). To agree on a thing, add i: Vi er enige i det (We agree on that).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **være enig** i det.
sentence.en: I can agree with that.

at være i tvivl.explanation: "At være i tvivl" means "to be in doubt", or to be unsure: Jeg er i tvivl om svaret (I am unsure about the answer). Use om (about) before the thing you are unsure of.

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **være i tvivl** om svaret.
sentence.en: You should not be in doubt about the answer.

at være kærester.explanation: "At være kærester" means "to be dating", or to be a couple: Vi har været kærester i to år (We have been a couple for two years). One person is en kæreste (a boyfriend or girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **være kærester** med dig.
sentence.en: I would like us to be a couple.

at være med.explanation: "At være med" means "to take part", to join what others are doing: Er du med? (Are you in?). It also means "to follow along": Jeg er ikke helt med (I am not quite following).

forms.en: to take part / be in on it
I take part / am in on it
I took part / was in on it
I have taken part / been in on it

sentence.da: Vil du **være med**, når vi spiller fodbold?
sentence.en: Do you want to join in when we play soccer?

at være nødt til.explanation: "At være nødt til" means "to have to", when you have no other choice: Jeg er nødt til at gå nu (I have to go now). It is stronger than skal (must / am going to), which can be just a plan: Jeg skal på arbejde (I am going to work).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **være nødt til** at vente.
sentence.en: I do not want to have to wait.

at være på vej.explanation: "At være på vej" means "to be on the way": Jeg er på vej hjem (I am on my way home). Before a place name, add til (to): Han er på vej til Aarhus (He is on his way to Aarhus).

forms.en: I have been on my way

sentence.da: Vi skal **være på vej** inden otte.
sentence.en: We must be on our way before eight.

at være syg.explanation: "At være syg" means "to be sick" or "to be ill": Jeg er syg (I am sick). To get sick, say at blive syg (to become sick): Jeg bliver syg (I am getting sick).

sentence.da: Jeg har feber og må **være syg** hjemme.
sentence.en: I have a fever and have to stay home sick.

at være træt af.explanation: "At være træt af" means "to be tired of", or fed up with something: Jeg er træt af regnen (I am tired of the rain). For sleepy tired, leave af out: Jeg er træt (I am sleepy).

sentence.da: Man kan let **være træt af** at vente.
sentence.en: You can easily get tired of waiting.

at være uenig.explanation: "At være uenig" means "to disagree" and is the opposite of agreeing: Jeg er uenig med dig (I disagree with you). To disagree about a thing, add i: Vi er uenige i det (We disagree on that).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **være uenig** med dig.
sentence.en: I do not want to disagree with you.

at være vant til.explanation: "At være vant til" means "to be used to", for something you have lived with for a long time: Hun er vant til støjen (She is used to the noise). After til, you can also use at plus a verb: Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op (I am used to getting up early).

sentence.da: Efter et år vil du **være vant til** kulden.
sentence.en: After a year, you will be used to the cold.

at være ved at.explanation: "At være ved at" means "to be about to" or "to be in the middle of": Toget er ved at køre (The train is about to leave). Jeg er ved at spise (I am in the middle of eating). The situation tells you which one it is.

forms.en: to be about to / be in the middle of
I am about to / am in the middle of
I was about to / was in the middle of
I have been about to / been in the middle of

sentence.da: Han ser ud til at **være ved at** falde i søvn.
sentence.en: He seems to be about to fall asleep.

at være vild med.explanation: "At være vild med" means "to be crazy about", so to like something a lot: Jeg er vild med pizza (I love pizza). It also works for people: Hun er vild med ham (She is crazy about him).

sentence.da: Du vil **være vild med** den her film.
sentence.en: You will love this movie.

at være væk.explanation: "At være væk" means "to be gone" or "to be away". It is used for people who are not there (Han er væk, He is gone) and for things that have disappeared (Min telefon er væk, My phone is gone).

sentence.da: Han skal **være væk** i to dage.
sentence.en: He has to be away for two days.

en vaccination.explanation: "En vaccination" means "a vaccination", a shot that protects you from a disease: Du skal have en vaccination til nogle lande (You need a vaccination for some countries). The shorter en vaccine is the medicine itself.

sentence.da: Børnene får en **vaccination** hos lægen.
sentence.en: The children get a vaccination at the doctor's.

en vaccine.explanation: "En vaccine" means "a vaccine", the injection that protects you from a disease. Mod (against) comes after it: en vaccine mod mæslinger (a vaccine against measles).

sentence.da: Lægen gav mig en **vaccine** mod influenza.
sentence.en: The doctor gave me a vaccine against the flu.

en vaffel.explanation: "En vaffel" means "a waffle", and also the crisp cone that holds ice cream: en is i vaffel (an ice cream in a cone).

sentence.da: Til dessert får jeg en **vaffel** med is.
sentence.en: For dessert I get a waffle with ice cream.

en vagt.explanation: "En vagt" means "a guard", and also "a shift" at work, for example in a hospital: Hun har vagt i weekenden (She is on duty this weekend). A security guard is en sikkerhedsvagt.

sentence.da: Han har **vagt** på hospitalet i nat.
sentence.en: He is on duty at the hospital tonight.

en valnød.explanation: "En valnød" means "a walnut", a nut with a hard shell. You crack it open: Man knækker en valnød med en nøddeknækker (You crack a walnut with a nutcracker).

sentence.da: Jeg knækker en **valnød** og spiser den.
sentence.en: I crack a walnut and eat it.

en vampyr.explanation: "En vampyr" means "a vampire", a creature in scary stories that drinks blood: Vampyren bor i et gammelt slot (The vampire lives in an old castle).

sentence.da: En **vampyr** drikker blod og sover om dagen.
sentence.en: A vampire drinks blood and sleeps during the day.

en vandflaske.explanation: "En vandflaske" means "a water bottle", the bottle you refill and carry with you: Husk din vandflaske (Remember your water bottle).

sentence.da: Jeg tager altid en **vandflaske** med på tur.
sentence.en: I always take a water bottle on trips.

en vandhane.explanation: "En vandhane" means "a faucet" or "a tap". It is built from vand (water) and hane (a tap or a rooster): Luk for vandhanen (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: Der drypper vand fra en **vandhane** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: Water is dripping from a faucet in the kitchen.

en vandkande.explanation: "En vandkande" means "a watering can". It is built from vand (water) and kande (jug): Jeg fylder vandkanden ved hanen (I fill the watering can at the tap).

sentence.da: Jeg vander blomsterne med en **vandkande**.
sentence.en: I water the flowers with a watering can.

en vandkaraffel.explanation: "En vandkaraffel" means "a water carafe", a jug for serving water at the table: Hun fylder vandkaraflen op (She fills up the water carafe).

sentence.da: Der står en **vandkaraffel** på bordet.
sentence.en: There is a water carafe on the table.

en vandmelon.explanation: "En vandmelon" means "a watermelon", built from vand (water) and melon. It is big, red inside, and full of water: Vi deler en vandmelon (We are sharing a watermelon).

sentence.da: På en varm dag spiser vi **vandmelon**.
sentence.en: On a warm day, we eat watermelon.

en vandpyt.explanation: "En vandpyt" means "a puddle", water that stays on the ground after rain: Børnene hopper i vandpytterne (The children jump in the puddles).

sentence.da: Jeg trådte i en stor **vandpyt** og blev våd.
sentence.en: I stepped in a big puddle and got wet.

en vandregning.explanation: "En vandregning" means "a water bill". It is vand (water) plus regning (bill): Min vandregning er høj i år (My water bill is high this year).

sentence.da: Vi sparer på vandet og får en lav **vandregning**.
sentence.en: We save on water and get a low water bill.

en vandretur.explanation: "En vandretur" means "a hike", a long walk in nature: Vi går en vandretur i skoven (We are going on a hike in the forest). It is built from at vandre (to hike) and tur (trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en lang **vandretur** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going on a long hike this weekend.

en vane.explanation: "En vane" means "a habit", something you do again and again: Det er en dårlig vane (It is a bad habit). You can also say what you usually do with for vane (as a habit): Jeg har for vane at gå en tur (I usually take a walk).

sentence.da: Det er en dårlig **vane** at komme for sent.
sentence.en: It is a bad habit to be late.

en vare.explanation: "En vare" means "an item" or "a product" that is for sale: Jeg leder efter en bestemt vare (I am looking for a certain item). For a thing you own, say en ting (a thing) instead.

sentence.da: Denne **vare** koster kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: This item costs only twenty kroner.

en vareprøve.explanation: "En vareprøve" means "a product sample", a small free amount to try at home: Butikken giver gratis vareprøver væk (The store gives away free samples).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **vareprøve** af den nye creme.
sentence.en: I got a product sample of the new cream.

en varevogn.explanation: "En varevogn" means "a van", a vehicle for carrying goods. It is built from varer (goods) and vogn (wagon): Håndværkeren kommer i en varevogn (The tradesman comes in a van).

sentence.da: Vi flytter vores møbler i en **varevogn**.
sentence.en: We are moving our furniture in a van.

en varmepumpe.explanation: "En varmepumpe" means "a heat pump". It is built from varme (heat) and pumpe (pump): Vi har en varmepumpe i huset (We have a heat pump in the house).

sentence.da: Vi varmer huset op med en **varmepumpe**.
sentence.en: We heat the house with a heat pump.

en vase.explanation: "En vase" means "a vase", for cut flowers: Blomsterne står i vasen (The flowers are in the vase).

sentence.da: Hun sætter blomsterne i en **vase** med vand.
sentence.en: She puts the flowers in a vase with water.

en vask.explanation: "En vask" means "a sink", in the bathroom or the kitchen: Der er kopper i vasken (There are cups in the sink). The word at vaske (to wash) looks almost the same but is an action: Jeg vasker hænder (I wash my hands).

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **vask** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We have a big sink in the kitchen.

en vaskekælder.explanation: "En vaskekælder" means "a laundry room" in the basement of a building. It is built from vaske (to wash) and kælder (basement): Vaskemaskinen står i vaskekælderen (The washing machine is in the laundry room).

sentence.da: Vores tøj vaskes i en **vaskekælder** under huset.
sentence.en: Our clothes are washed in a laundry room under the house.

en vaskemaskine.explanation: "En vaskemaskine" means "a washing machine" for clothes: Tøjet er i vaskemaskinen (The clothes are in the washing machine). Jeg sætter vaskemaskinen i gang (I start the washing machine).

sentence.da: Min **vaskemaskine** larmer meget i dag.
sentence.en: My washing machine is very noisy today.

en vatpind.explanation: "En vatpind" means "a cotton swab". It is built from vat (cotton wool) and en pind (a stick), so it is a small stick with cotton on the end.

sentence.da: Hun renser sin telefon med en **vatpind**.
sentence.en: She cleans her phone with a cotton swab.

en veganer.explanation: "En veganer" means "a vegan", a person who eats no meat, fish, eggs or dairy: Min bror er veganer (My brother is a vegan). It is different from a vegetarian, who may still eat eggs and dairy.

sentence.da: Hun er **veganer** og spiser hverken kød eller ost.
sentence.en: She is a vegan and eats neither meat nor cheese.

en vegetar.explanation: "En vegetar" means "a vegetarian", a person who does not eat meat. To say what you are, use Jeg er vegetar (I am a vegetarian). For food, use vegetarisk, as in en vegetarisk ret (a vegetarian dish).

sentence.da: Jeg er **vegetar** og spiser ikke kød.
sentence.en: I am a vegetarian and do not eat meat.

en vej.explanation: "En vej" means "a road" and also "a way" or route: Hvilken vej skal jeg gå? means "Which way should I go?". At spørge om vej means "to ask for directions", with no en before vej.

sentence.da: Bilen kører på en lang **vej**.
sentence.en: The car drives on a long road.

en vejledning.explanation: "En vejledning" means "a guide / guidance", help or instructions that show you how to do something: Læs vejledningen først (Read the guide first). A person who gives guidance is en vejleder (an advisor).

sentence.da: Du kan finde en **vejledning** på hjemmesiden.
sentence.en: You can find a guide on the website.

en vejrmelding.explanation: "En vejrmelding" means "a weather report". It is built from vejr (weather) and melding (message). Jeg tjekker vejrmeldingen hver morgen (I check the weather report every morning).

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til en **vejrmelding** om regn i morgen.
sentence.en: I listen to a weather report about rain tomorrow.

en vejrudsigt.explanation: "En vejrudsigt" means "a weather forecast", a description of what the weather will be like. It is made from vejr (weather) and udsigt (outlook).

sentence.da: Jeg ser en **vejrudsigt** om regn i morgen.
sentence.en: I see a weather forecast about rain tomorrow.

en ven.explanation: "En ven" means "a friend", usually a male friend, but it can be used for a friend of either sex. Be careful with kæreste (boyfriend or girlfriend): it means a romantic partner, not just a friend.

sentence.da: Jeg spiller fodbold med min **ven**.
sentence.en: I play soccer with my friend.

en veninde.explanation: "En veninde" means "a female friend", used when the friend is a woman or girl. For a male friend, or a friend in general, use en ven (a friend).

sentence.da: Min **veninde** er en sød pige.
sentence.en: My female friend is a nice girl.

en vennegruppe.explanation: "En vennegruppe" means "a group of friends", built from venner (friends) and gruppe (group): Jeg har en stor vennegruppe i Aarhus (I have a big group of friends in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Min **vennegruppe** mødes hver fredag.
sentence.en: My group of friends meets every Friday.

en venteliste.explanation: "En venteliste" means "a waiting list": the list you are put on when something is full. Du er nummer tre på ventelisten (You are number three on the waiting list).

sentence.da: Vi står på **venteliste** til en plads i børnehaven.
sentence.en: We are on the waiting list for a spot in kindergarten.

en ventetid.explanation: "En ventetid" means "a wait time", how long you wait for something: Ventetiden hos lægen er to timer (The wait at the doctor is two hours). It is built from at vente (to wait) and en tid (a time).

sentence.da: Der er lang **ventetid** hos lægen.
sentence.en: There is a long wait at the doctor.

en ventilator.explanation: "En ventilator" means "a fan" that moves air: Ventilatoren støjer (The fan is noisy). A fan of a team or a singer is en fan, not en ventilator.

sentence.da: Det er varmt, og jeg tænder en **ventilator**.
sentence.en: It is hot, and I am turning on a fan.

en verden.explanation: "En verden" means "a world". Common phrases are i hele verden (all over the world) and verdens bedste (the best in the world), where verdens means "the world's".

sentence.da: En **verden** uden musik ville være stille.
sentence.en: A world without music would be quiet.

en version.explanation: "En version" means "a version", one form of something: Det er den nyeste version af appen (It is the newest version of the app). It also fits stories: Hun fortalte sin version (She told her version).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger den nyeste **version** af appen.
sentence.en: I use the newest version of the app.

en vest.explanation: "En vest" means "a vest", a piece of clothing without sleeves, often worn over a shirt: Jeg har en varm vest på (I am wearing a warm vest).

sentence.da: Min onkel har en grå **vest** over skjorten.
sentence.en: My uncle has a gray vest over his shirt.

en videnskabsmand.explanation: "En videnskabsmand" means "a scientist". It is built from videnskab (science) and mand (man): Han er videnskabsmand (He is a scientist).

sentence.da: Den kendte **videnskabsmand** arbejder på et laboratorium.
sentence.en: The famous scientist works at a laboratory.

en video.explanation: "En video" means "a video", a short clip or a longer film online: Jeg ser en video om mad (I am watching a video about food). To make one, say at optage en video (to record a video).

sentence.da: Jeg har set en sjov **video** på nettet.
sentence.en: I watched a funny video online.

en vielsesring.explanation: "En vielsesring" means "a wedding ring", the ring a married person wears: Hun har altid sin vielsesring på (She always wears her wedding ring). Do not mix it up with en forlovelsesring (an engagement ring).

sentence.da: Han har en **vielsesring** på fingeren.
sentence.en: He has a wedding ring on his finger.

en vikar.explanation: "En vikar" means "a substitute teacher", someone who steps in when the regular teacher is away: Vi har en vikar i dag (We have a substitute today). It also works for other jobs: en vikar på kontoret (a temp at the office).

sentence.da: Vi får en **vikar**, fordi vores lærer er syg.
sentence.en: We get a substitute because our teacher is sick.

en viking.explanation: "En viking" means "a Viking", a Scandinavian sailor-warrior from long ago: Vikingerne boede i Danmark for mange år siden (The Vikings lived in Denmark many years ago).

sentence.da: En **viking** sejlede over havet i et langt skib.
sentence.en: A Viking sailed over the sea in a long ship.

en vilje.explanation: "En vilje" means "a will", the drive to want something: Jeg gjorde det ikke med vilje (I did not do it on purpose). Hvor der er en vilje, er der en vej (Where there is a will, there is a way).

sentence.da: Det kræver **vilje** at holde op med at ryge.
sentence.en: It takes willpower to quit smoking.

en villa.explanation: "En villa" means "a detached house", a house that stands alone with its own garden: Vi bor i en villa (We live in a detached house). It does not have to be fancy.

sentence.da: De bor i en stor **villa** med have.
sentence.en: They live in a big detached house with a garden.

en vin.explanation: "En vin" means "a wine". You can name the color: en rødvin (a red wine) or en hvidvin (a white wine). To order, say et glas vin (a glass of wine) or en flaske vin (a bottle of wine).

sentence.da: Vi bestiller en flaske **vin** til maden.
sentence.en: We order a bottle of wine for the meal.

en vinbar.explanation: "En vinbar" means "a wine bar", a place that serves wine by the glass: Vi mødes på en vinbar (We are meeting at a wine bar).

sentence.da: Vi drikker rødvin på en hyggelig **vinbar**.
sentence.en: We drink red wine at a cozy wine bar.

en vinder.explanation: "En vinder" means "a winner", the person or team that wins: Vinderen får en pokal (The winner gets a trophy). The one who loses is en taber (a loser).

sentence.da: Hvem bliver **vinder** af kampen i aften?
sentence.en: Who will be the winner of the match tonight?

en vindmølle.explanation: "En vindmølle" means "a wind turbine" or "a windmill", the tall machine that turns in the wind: Der står mange vindmøller langs kysten (Many wind turbines stand along the coast).

sentence.da: Vi kan se en stor **vindmølle** fra vinduet.
sentence.en: We can see a big wind turbine from the window.

en vindrue.explanation: "En vindrue" means "a grape", and en drue (a grape) means the same: Jeg køber røde vindruer (I buy red grapes). The word starts with vin (wine), but these grapes are for eating too.

sentence.da: Han spiser en grøn **vindrue** ad gangen.
sentence.en: He eats one green grape at a time.

en vindueskarm.explanation: "En vindueskarm" means "a windowsill", the flat ledge at the bottom of a window. Danish says i (in) for it: Katten sidder i vindueskarmen (The cat sits on the windowsill).

sentence.da: Der står en lille plante i hver **vindueskarm**.
sentence.en: There is a small plant on every windowsill.

en vinduesplads.explanation: "En vinduesplads" means "a window seat" on a plane, bus or train: Kan jeg få en vinduesplads i stedet? (Can I get a window seat instead?) Its opposite is en gangplads (an aisle seat).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **vinduesplads**.
sentence.en: I would like a window seat.

en vinduesvisker.explanation: "En vinduesvisker" means "a windshield wiper": Vinduesviskeren virker ikke (The wiper does not work). It is vindue (window) plus visker (wiper).

sentence.da: Det regner meget, og min **vinduesvisker** går hurtigt.
sentence.en: It is raining a lot, and my wiper moves fast.

en vinkel.explanation: "En vinkel" means "an angle", in math and in how you look at things: Trekanten har tre vinkler (The triangle has three angles). Jeg ser det fra en anden vinkel (I see it from another angle).

sentence.da: Her er en **vinkel** på halvfems grader.
sentence.en: Here is an angle of ninety degrees.

en vinliste.explanation: "En vinliste" means "a wine list", the menu of wines at a restaurant. It is built from vin (wine) and liste (list): Må jeg se vinlisten? (May I see the wine list?)

sentence.da: Må jeg få en **vinliste**, tak?
sentence.en: May I have a wine list, please?

en vinter.explanation: "En vinter" means "a winter". Use om vinteren for "in the winter" in general, and "i vinter" for "this winter".

sentence.da: En **vinter** i Danmark er kold og mørk.
sentence.en: A winter in Denmark is cold and dark.

en vinterbader.explanation: "En vinterbader" means "a winter swimmer", a person who swims in the sea or a lake in the cold months: Hun er vinterbader (She is a winter swimmer). It is built from vinter (winter) and at bade (to bathe).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **vinterbader** og svømmer i havet hver morgen.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a winter swimmer and swims in the sea every morning.

en vinterdag.explanation: "En vinterdag" means "a winter day". It is built from vinter (winter) and dag (day): Børnene leger i sneen på en kold vinterdag (The children play in the snow on a cold winter day).

sentence.da: Det er en kold **vinterdag**, og det sner.
sentence.en: It is a cold winter day, and it is snowing.

en vinterjakke.explanation: "En vinterjakke" means "a winter jacket". It is made from vinter (winter) and jakke (jacket).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **vinterjakke** på.
sentence.en: I am wearing a warm winter jacket.

en vinternat.explanation: "En vinternat" means "a winter night". It is built from vinter (winter) and nat (night): Vi gik hjem på en kold vinternat (We walked home on a cold winter night).

sentence.da: Det er koldt og mørkt på en **vinternat**.
sentence.en: It is cold and dark on a winter night.

en vinterstøvle.explanation: "En vinterstøvle" means "a winter boot", a warm boot for snow and cold. You usually say it in the plural: Jeg tager vinterstøvler på (I put on winter boots).

sentence.da: Min venstre **vinterstøvle** er våd af sne.
sentence.en: My left winter boot is wet from snow.

en violin.explanation: "En violin" means "a violin". Danish also has en fiol (a fiddle), often used for folk music: Han spiller fiol til dans (He plays fiddle for dancing).

sentence.da: Min datter øver sig på **violin** hver dag.
sentence.en: My daughter practices the violin every day.

en virkelighed.explanation: "En virkelighed" means "a reality", what is real, as opposed to what you imagine: Drømmen blev til virkelighed (The dream became reality). Han lever ikke i virkeligheden (He does not live in the real world).

sentence.da: Hendes plan blev til **virkelighed** i sommer.
sentence.en: Her plan became reality this summer.

en virksomhed.explanation: "En virksomhed" means "a business", a company seen as an organization with workers: Virksomheden har tyve ansatte (The business has twenty employees). Mange virksomheder lukker i juli (Many businesses close in July).

sentence.da: Hun driver en lille **virksomhed** med fem ansatte.
sentence.en: She runs a small business with five employees.

en virus.explanation: "En virus" means "a virus", both for illness and for computers: Min computer har fået en virus (My computer has caught a virus). Jeg har en virus (I have a virus) means you are sick.

sentence.da: Min computer har fået en **virus** fra en e-mail.
sentence.en: My computer got a virus from an email.

en vissen blomst.explanation: "En vissen blomst" means "a withered flower", one that has dried up and drooped: Blomsterne blev visne uden vand (The flowers became withered without water).

sentence.da: Der står en **vissen blomst** i vasen.
sentence.en: There is a withered flower in the vase.

en vitamin.explanation: "En vitamin" means "a vitamin": Jeg tager en vitamin hver dag (I take a vitamin every day). A named one puts the letter first: C-vitamin (vitamin C).

sentence.da: Hun tager en **vitamin** hver morgen.
sentence.en: She takes a vitamin every morning.

en vits.explanation: "En vits" means "a joke", a short funny story with a punchline: Jeg kender en god vits (I know a good joke). The surprise at the end is called en pointe (a punchline).

sentence.da: Min lærer fortæller en sjov **vits** hver fredag.
sentence.en: My teacher tells a funny joke every Friday.

en vittighed.explanation: "En vittighed" means "a joke", the same as en vits (a joke): Det var en god vittighed (That was a good joke). It can sound a little more formal.

sentence.da: Han fortæller en sjov **vittighed** til alle.
sentence.en: He tells everyone a funny joke.

en vogn.explanation: "En vogn" means "a wagon" or "a cart", a vehicle on wheels: Hestene trækker vognen (The horses pull the wagon). Maden står på en vogn (The food is on a cart).

sentence.da: Hesten trækker en tung **vogn** op ad bakken.
sentence.en: The horse pulls a heavy wagon up the hill.

en voksen.explanation: "En voksen" means "an adult": Voksne betaler hundrede kroner (Adults pay a hundred kroner). The word comes from at vokse (to grow), so it is someone who has grown up.

sentence.da: En **voksen** skal følge børnene hjem.
sentence.en: An adult must walk the children home.

en vugge.explanation: "En vugge" means "a cradle", a small bed for a baby that rocks: Babyen sover i vuggen (The baby sleeps in the cradle). The same word is the verb at vugge (to rock).

sentence.da: Den lille baby sover i en **vugge** ved sengen.
sentence.en: The little baby sleeps in a cradle next to the bed.

en vulkan.explanation: "En vulkan" means "a volcano": Vulkanen er farlig (The volcano is dangerous). An eruption is et vulkanudbrud (a volcanic eruption).

sentence.da: Der kommer varm lava ud af en **vulkan**.
sentence.en: Hot lava comes out of a volcano.

en væg.explanation: "En væg" means "a wall" inside a building or room. For a wall outdoors, such as around a garden, Danes say en mur (a brick or stone wall).

sentence.da: Billedet hænger på en **væg**.
sentence.en: The picture hangs on a wall.

en vægt.explanation: "En vægt" means "a weight": Hvad er din vægt? (What is your weight?) It is also the machine you stand on to weigh yourself, a scale: Vægten står på badeværelset (The scale is in the bathroom).

sentence.da: Kufferten har en **vægt** på tyve kilo.
sentence.en: The suitcase has a weight of twenty kilos.

en vært.explanation: "En vært" means "a host", the person who invites guests to their home: Værten laver mad til alle (The host makes food for everyone). It also means the host of a show: Hun er vært på et tv-program (She is the host of a TV show).

sentence.da: Vores **vært** tog imod os ved døren.
sentence.en: Our host welcomed us at the door.

en værtindegave.explanation: "En værtindegave" means "a hostess gift", a small present you bring to the host of a dinner: Jeg tog vin med som værtindegave (I brought wine as a hostess gift). It is built from værtinde (hostess) and gave (gift).

sentence.da: Jeg tog blomster med som **værtindegave**.
sentence.en: I brought flowers as a hostess gift.

en væske.explanation: "En væske" means "a liquid" or "a fluid": Vand er en væske (Water is a liquid). Doctors also use it for what you drink: Drik meget væske (Drink a lot of fluids).

sentence.da: Der løber en **væske** ud af flasken.
sentence.en: A liquid is running out of the bottle.

et valg.explanation: "Et valg" means "a choice" and also "an election": Det er dit valg (It is your choice). Der er valg i år (There is an election this year).

sentence.da: Du har et **valg**: te eller kaffe?
sentence.en: You have a choice: tea or coffee?

et vandfald.explanation: "Et vandfald" means "a waterfall". It is built from vand (water) and fald (a fall). Vi gik hen til vandfaldet (We walked over to the waterfall).

sentence.da: Vi hørte et stort **vandfald** i skoven.
sentence.en: We heard a big waterfall in the forest.

et vandrerhjem.explanation: "Et vandrerhjem" means "a hostel", a cheap place to stay. It is built from vandrer (hiker) and hjem (home), so literally a hiker's home.

sentence.da: Vi bor billigt på et **vandrerhjem**.
sentence.en: We stay cheaply at a hostel.

et vareudvalg.explanation: "Et vareudvalg" means "a range of goods", how many different things a shop offers: Et godt vareudvalg gør det nemt at finde noget (A good range makes it easy to find something).

sentence.da: Butikken har et stort **vareudvalg** og lave priser.
sentence.en: The store has a large range of goods and low prices.

et vaskemærke.explanation: "Et vaskemærke" means "a care label", the tag in clothes that says how to wash them. It is built from vaske (wash) and mærke (label): Det står på vaskemærket (It says so on the care label).

sentence.da: Der står 30 grader på det lille **vaskemærke**.
sentence.en: It says 30 degrees on the little care label.

et vaskeri.explanation: "Et vaskeri" means "a laundromat", a place outside your home where you wash clothes. A laundry room inside your own building is et fællesvaskeri (a shared laundry room).

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen vaskemaskine og vasker på et **vaskeri**.
sentence.en: I have no washing machine and wash at a laundromat.

et vaskerum.explanation: "Et vaskerum" means "a laundry room", a room for washing clothes, often shared in an apartment building: Naboen er i vaskerummet (The neighbor is in the laundry room).

sentence.da: Vi har et fælles **vaskerum** i kælderen.
sentence.en: We have a shared laundry room in the basement.

et vejskilt.explanation: "Et vejskilt" means "a road sign", the kind that shows a direction or a speed limit: Vejskiltet viser mod Aarhus (The road sign points toward Aarhus). Jeg kan ikke læse vejskiltet (I can't read the road sign).

sentence.da: Der står et **vejskilt** ved krydset.
sentence.en: There is a road sign at the intersection.

et venskab.explanation: "Et venskab" means "a friendship". It is built from ven (friend): Vores venskab er meget vigtigt for mig (Our friendship is very important to me).

sentence.da: Deres **venskab** har holdt i mange år.
sentence.en: Their friendship has lasted for many years.

et venteværelse.explanation: "Et venteværelse" means "a waiting room". It is built from at vente (to wait) and et værelse (a room). Sid i venteværelset (Sit in the waiting room).

sentence.da: Vi venter på lægen i et **venteværelse**.
sentence.en: We wait for the doctor in a waiting room.

et videoopkald.explanation: "Et videoopkald" means "a video call". It is built from video (video) and opkald (call): Vi har et videoopkald klokken tre (We have a video call at three o'clock).

sentence.da: Jeg ser min mormor i et **videoopkald** hver søndag.
sentence.en: I see my grandmother in a video call every Sunday.

et vidne.explanation: "Et vidne" means "a witness", someone who saw what happened: Der var tre vidner til ulykken (There were three witnesses to the accident). A witness is a person, while et bevis (a piece of evidence) is a thing.

sentence.da: Et **vidne** så bilen køre væk.
sentence.en: A witness saw the car drive away.

et vindue.explanation: "Et vindue" means "a window". Jeg åbner vinduet means "I open the window" and "Jeg lukker vinduet" means "I close the window".

sentence.da: Jeg åbner et **vindue** i stuen.
sentence.en: I open a window in the living room.

et vinglas.explanation: "Et vinglas" means "a wine glass", the glass with a stem used for wine: Der står et vinglas på bordet (There is a wine glass on the table).

sentence.da: Hun hælder rødvin i et **vinglas**.
sentence.en: She pours red wine into a wine glass.

et viskelæder.explanation: "Et viskelæder" means "an eraser", used to rub out pencil marks: Kan jeg låne dit viskelæder? (Can I borrow your eraser?) The word is built from viske (to wipe) and læder (leather).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **viskelæder**, når jeg skriver forkert.
sentence.en: I use an eraser when I write something wrong.

et viskestykke.explanation: "Et viskestykke" means "a dish towel", the cloth you use to dry dishes: Jeg tørrer glasset med viskestykket (I dry the glass with the dish towel).

sentence.da: Jeg tørrer tallerkenerne af med et **viskestykke**.
sentence.en: I dry the plates with a dish towel.

et visum.explanation: "Et visum" means "a visa", permission to enter or stay in a country. You apply for one with at søge om (to apply for): Jeg søger om et visum means "I am applying for a visa".

sentence.da: Jeg søger om et **visum** til Danmark.
sentence.en: I am applying for a visa to Denmark.

et vækkeur.explanation: "Et vækkeur" means "an alarm clock". It is built from at vække (to wake someone) and et ur (a clock). The alarm on a phone is en alarm (an alarm).

sentence.da: Jeg stiller mit **vækkeur** på seks.
sentence.en: I set my alarm clock to six.

et værelse.explanation: "Et værelse" means "a room" in a home or hotel. For room in the sense of free space, say plads (space): Der er plads (There is room).

sentence.da: Jeg har booket et **værelse** til to nætter.
sentence.en: I have booked a room for two nights.

et værksted.explanation: "Et værksted" means "a workshop", and also "a garage" where cars are repaired: Bilen står på værkstedet (The car is at the garage). A garage for parking is en garage (a garage).

sentence.da: Bilen skal repareres på et **værksted**.
sentence.en: The car has to be repaired at a workshop.

et værktøj.explanation: "Et værktøj" means "a tool". It is also used for tools as a group: Jeg har værktøj i skuret (I have tools in the shed).

sentence.da: En hammer er et nyttigt **værktøj**.
sentence.en: A hammer is a useful tool.

vand.explanation: "Vand" means "water". For water in general, you do not need a word for "a": Jeg drikker vand (I drink water). In a restaurant, you can also ask Må jeg få et glas vand? (May I have a glass of water?), or ask for koldt vand (cold water).

sentence.da: Må jeg bede om et glas **vand**?
sentence.en: May I have a glass of water?

vanilje.explanation: "Vanilje" means "vanilla", a sweet taste used in cakes and desserts: Vi bruger vanilje i kagen (We use vanilla in the cake). For ice cream, say vaniljeis (vanilla ice cream).

sentence.da: Kagen smager af **vanilje**.
sentence.en: The cake tastes of vanilla.

vanskelig.explanation: "Vanskelig" means "difficult" and describes tasks, questions and situations: et vanskeligt spørgsmål (a difficult question). It is a little more formal than svær (hard).

sentence.da: Det er en **vanskelig** opgave.
sentence.en: It is a difficult task.

vant til.explanation: "Vant til" means "used to" in the sense of "accustomed to": Jeg er vant til kulden (I am used to the cold). For a past habit, use plejede at: Jeg plejede at bo i Aarhus (I used to live in Aarhus).

forms.da: Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op.
forms.en: I am used to getting up early.

forms.da: Han er vant til hårdt arbejde.
forms.en: He is used to hard work.
We are used to the rain.

sentence.da: Jeg er **vant til** at cykle hver dag.
sentence.en: I am used to biking every day.

vanvittig.explanation: "Vanvittig" means "crazy" or "insane", and stresses that something is extreme: en vanvittig idé (a crazy idea). It also works as a strong complaint: Det er vanvittigt dyrt (It is insanely expensive).

sentence.da: Det er en **vanvittig** idé, men jeg kan lide den.
sentence.en: It is a crazy idea, but I like it.

varm.explanation: "Varm" means both warm and "hot", for weather, food, drinks and rooms: varm kaffe (hot coffee) and varm mad (hot food).

sentence.da: Suppen er **varm** og god.
sentence.en: The soup is hot and good.

varme.explanation: "En varme" means "heat" or "warmth". The same spelling also appears in at varme (to heat up) and varme dage (warm days), so the rest of the sentence tells you which one is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke tåle **varme**.
sentence.en: I can't stand heat.

vaskepulver.explanation: "Vaskepulver" means "laundry detergent" in powder form. It is for clothes, so do not use it on plates: for those, say opvaskemiddel (dish soap).

sentence.da: Jeg putter **vaskepulver** i vaskemaskinen.
sentence.en: I put laundry detergent in the washing machine.

vasketøj.explanation: "Vasketøj" means "laundry", the clothes that need washing. It is built from at vaske (to wash) and tøj (clothes): Jeg folder vasketøjet (I am folding the laundry).

sentence.da: Jeg har meget **vasketøj** i dag.
sentence.en: I have a lot of laundry today.

ved.explanation: "Ved" means "by" or "at". Compare Han sidder ved vinduet (He sits by the window) with Vi sidder ved bordet (We sit at the table). Careful: ved also means "know" in Jeg ved det (I know it). The rest of the sentence shows which one it is.

sentence.da: Vi mødes **ved** stationen.
sentence.en: We are meeting at the station.

ved siden af.explanation: "Ved siden af" means "next to": Stolen står ved siden af bordet (The chair is next to the table). It can also mean "alongside": ved siden af mit arbejde (alongside my job).

sentence.da: Banken ligger **ved siden af** posthuset.
sentence.en: The bank is next to the post office.

vegansk.explanation: "Vegansk" means "vegan", with no meat, fish, eggs or dairy: Burgeren er vegansk (The burger is vegan). A person who eats this way is en veganer (a vegan).

sentence.da: Jeg bager en **vegansk** kage uden æg og smør.
sentence.en: I am baking a vegan cake without eggs or butter.

vegetarisk.explanation: "Vegetarisk" means "vegetarian" (without meat) and describes food. In a restaurant, you can ask Har I noget vegetarisk? (Do you have anything vegetarian?). For a person who is a vegetarian, say en vegetar (a vegetarian).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser ikke kød. En **vegetarisk** ret, tak.
sentence.en: I don't eat meat. A vegetarian dish, please.

vejarbejde.explanation: "Vejarbejde" means "roadworks", the work done on a road: Der er vejarbejde på motorvejen (There are roadworks on the highway). Vi holder i kø på grund af vejarbejde (We are stuck in a line because of roadworks).

sentence.da: Vi kommer for sent, fordi der er **vejarbejde**.
sentence.en: We will be late because there are roadworks.

vejr.explanation: "Vejr" means "weather". You can ask Hvordan er vejret? (How is the weather?) and answer Det er koldt i dag (It is cold today) or Det er dårligt vejr (It is bad weather).

sentence.da: Det er godt **vejr** i dag.
sentence.en: The weather is good today.

vel.explanation: "Vel" means "I suppose" or "surely". It softens a guess or a question, often hoping for a yes: Det er vel i orden (I suppose that is fine).

forms.en: You are not sick, are you?
He is probably home by now.
I suppose it does not cost much.

sentence.da: Du kommer **vel** i morgen?
sentence.en: You are coming tomorrow, right?

velbekomme.explanation: "Velbekomme" means "enjoy your meal" when you serve food, and "you're welcome" when someone says tak for mad (thanks for the meal). It is only used about food and drink. For other thanks, say selv tak (you're welcome) or det var så lidt (it was nothing).

forms.en: Thanks for the meal. You're welcome.

sentence.da: Her er suppen. **Velbekomme**!
sentence.en: Here is the soup. Enjoy!

velkommen.explanation: "Velkommen" means "welcome". Use it to greet guests, adding til (to) and the place: velkommen til Danmark (welcome to Denmark). Do not use it for "you're welcome", which is selv tak or det var så lidt (it was nothing).

sentence.da: **Velkommen** til vores hjem!
sentence.en: Welcome to our home!

venlig.explanation: "Venlig" means "friendly" or "kind", for people, voices and smiles. Venlig hilsen (kind regards) is how you end a letter or an email.

sentence.da: Hun er **venlig** og smiler til mig.
sentence.en: She is friendly and smiles at me.

venlighed.explanation: "Venlighed" means "kindness", being nice to other people: Tak for din venlighed (Thank you for your kindness). Hendes venlighed gjorde mig glad (Her kindness made me happy).

sentence.da: Vi mødte stor **venlighed** på rejsen.
sentence.en: We met great kindness on the trip.

venligst.explanation: "Venligst" means "please" in a formal way and is common on signs and in letters: Luk døren venligst (Please close the door).

sentence.da: Husk **venligst** at lukke døren.
sentence.en: Please remember to close the door.

venstre.explanation: "Venstre" means "left", as in the left side or the left hand. In directions, you usually say til venstre (to the left).

sentence.da: Tag den første vej til **venstre**.
sentence.en: Take the first road on the left.

vent lidt.explanation: "Vent lidt" means "wait a bit". Lidt (a little) softens the request, and adding tak (thanks / please) makes it more polite.

sentence.da: Jeg finder min taske. **Vent lidt**!
sentence.en: I'm looking for my bag. Wait a bit!

vest.explanation: "Vest" means "west": Vinden kommer fra vest (The wind comes from the west). It is also part of place names such as Vestjylland (western Jutland, the western part of the Danish mainland).

sentence.da: Solen går ned i **vest**.
sentence.en: The sun goes down in the west.

vestlig.explanation: "Vestlig" means "western" and also "from the west": en vestlig vind (a westerly wind). Esbjerg ligger i det vestlige Danmark (Esbjerg is in western Denmark).

sentence.da: Vinden kommer fra en **vestlig** retning.
sentence.en: The wind comes from a westerly direction.

vestpå.explanation: "Vestpå" means "westward", toward the west, for movement: Flyet drejer vestpå (The plane turns west). For a place, use vest for (west of): Esbjerg ligger vest for Odense (Esbjerg is west of Odense).

sentence.da: Toget kører **vestpå** mod Esbjerg.
sentence.en: The train goes west toward Esbjerg.

vi.explanation: "Vi" means "we", as in Vi bor her (We live here). After a word like ser (sees), we becomes os (us): Vi ser ham (We see him) but Han ser os (He sees us).

sentence.da: I dag spiser **vi** hjemme.
sentence.en: Today we eat at home.

vi ses.explanation: "Vi ses" means "see you" and is the everyday way to say goodbye. It is short for "we see each other". Add a time to be specific: vi ses i morgen (see you tomorrow) or vi ses på fredag (see you on Friday). In a more formal setting, use på gensyn (see you again).

sentence.da: Jeg skal gå nu. **Vi ses** i morgen!
sentence.en: I have to go now. See you tomorrow!

vi snakkes.explanation: "Vi snakkes" means "talk to you later" and is a casual goodbye between people who will speak again soon. It is common on the phone and in messages: Tak for hjælpen, vi snakkes! (Thanks for the help, talk to you later!)

sentence.da: Jeg har travlt nu, men **vi snakkes**.
sentence.en: I'm busy now, but talk to you later.

vi tales ved.explanation: "Vi tales ved" means "we'll talk" and is a friendly goodbye, mostly after a phone call or message, when you expect to speak again soon. Use vi ses (see you) instead when you expect to meet in person.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer i aften. **Vi tales ved**!
sentence.en: I'll call tonight. Talk soon!

via.explanation: "Via" means "by way of" or "through": Vi kører via Odense (We drive by way of Odense). It also fits ways of reaching someone: Skriv til mig via mail (Write to me via email).

sentence.da: Vi rejser **via** København til Aarhus.
sentence.en: We travel via Copenhagen to Aarhus.

viden.explanation: "Viden" means "knowledge", everything a person knows about something: Hun har meget viden om dyr (She has a lot of knowledge about animals). Viden er magt (Knowledge is power).

sentence.da: Hun har meget **viden** om historie.
sentence.en: She has a lot of knowledge about history.

vidunderlig.explanation: "Vidunderlig" means "wonderful", and is stronger than god (good): Vejret er vidunderligt (The weather is wonderful).

sentence.da: Vi har haft en **vidunderlig** ferie.
sentence.en: We have had a wonderful vacation.

vigtig.explanation: "Vigtig" means "important", for things, people, news and decisions: en vigtig beslutning (an important decision).

sentence.da: I morgen er en **vigtig** dag.
sentence.en: Tomorrow is an important day.

vild.explanation: "Vild" means "wild": vilde blomster (wild flowers). In everyday talk it also means "awesome" or "crazy": Den fest var vild (That party was awesome).

sentence.da: Hesten var **vild**, men nu er den rolig.
sentence.en: The horse was wild, but now it is calm.

vild med.explanation: "Vild med" means "crazy about", for things and people you really like: Jeg er vild med pizza (I am crazy about pizza). It goes after er (am/is/are).

sentence.da: Min søn er **vild med** fodbold.
sentence.en: My son is crazy about soccer.

vildt.explanation: "Vildt" means "wild" and goes with et-words: et vildt dyr (a wild animal). In everyday talk, Det var vildt! means "That was crazy!", often in a good way.

sentence.da: En ræv er et **vildt** dyr.
sentence.en: A fox is a wild animal.

villig.explanation: "Villig" means "willing", for being ready to do something: Jeg er villig til at hjælpe (I am willing to help).

sentence.da: Hun er **villig** til at vente lidt.
sentence.en: She is willing to wait a little.

vind.explanation: "Vind" means "wind". To say it is windy, Danes use at blæse (to blow): Det blæser (It is windy).

sentence.da: Der er meget **vind** i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of wind today.

virkelig.explanation: "Virkelig" means "really". Compare Det er godt (It is good) with Det er virkelig godt (It is really good). On its own, Virkelig? (Really?) shows surprise.

sentence.da: Maden er **virkelig** god.
sentence.en: The food is really good.

vist.explanation: "Vist" means "probably" or "I think" and softens a guess: Han er vist syg (He is probably sick). It sounds less sure than a plain statement.

forms.en: I do not think we have milk

sentence.da: Han er **vist** hjemme nu.
sentence.en: I think he is home now.

voksen.explanation: "Voksen" means "grown-up" or "adult": Min bror er voksen nu (My brother is an adult now). The same word also names the person: en voksen (an adult).

sentence.da: Min datter er **voksen** nu og bor i Aarhus.
sentence.en: My daughter is an adult now and lives in Aarhus.

volleyball.explanation: "Volleyball" means "volleyball". To say you play it, use spille (to play): Vi spiller volleyball hver fredag (We play volleyball every Friday).

sentence.da: Vi spiller **volleyball** på stranden om sommeren.
sentence.en: We play volleyball on the beach in the summer.

vores.explanation: "Vores" means "our". Compare Det er mit hus (It is my house) with Det er vores hus (It is our house). It never changes: vores bil (our car), vores børn (our children).

sentence.da: **Vores** hus er meget stort.
sentence.en: Our house is very big.

vred.explanation: "Vred" means "angry". To say you are angry at someone, use vred på (angry at): Jeg er vred på ham (I am angry at him). It is fairly strong; for being a little annoyed Danes use irriteret (annoyed) or sur (grumpy).

sentence.da: Han er meget **vred** på mig.
sentence.en: He is very angry at me.

vred på.explanation: "Vred på" means "angry at": Hun er vred på sin chef (She is angry at her boss). It is a bit stronger than sur på (mad at).

forms.da: Jeg er vred på mig selv.

forms.en: They are angry at each other.

sentence.da: Hun er **vred på** sin bror, fordi han løj.
sentence.en: She is angry at her brother because he lied.

vrøvl.explanation: "Vrøvl" means "nonsense": Han snakker vrøvl (He is talking nonsense). It is direct, so it fits friends better than strangers.

sentence.da: Det er noget **vrøvl**, og jeg tror ikke på det.
sentence.en: That is nonsense, and I do not believe it.

våd.explanation: "Våd" means "wet", for clothes, hair, the ground, or anything soaked with water: Det regner, så jakken er våd (It is raining, so the jacket is wet).

sentence.da: Hunden er helt **våd** af regn.
sentence.en: The dog is completely wet from rain.

vågen.explanation: "Vågen" means "awake": Er du vågen? (Are you awake?) Do not mix it up with at vågne (to wake up): Jeg vågnede klokken syv (I woke up at seven).

sentence.da: Jeg er **vågen** hele natten.
sentence.en: I am awake all night.

væk.explanation: "Væk" means "away" or "gone". Compare Hun løber væk (She runs away) with Min nøgle er væk (My key is gone). Tag den væk (Take it away) is fine, but Gå væk! (Go away!) sounds rude.

sentence.da: Min taske er **væk**!
sentence.en: My bag is gone!

vældig.explanation: "Vældig" means "very" or "really", a friendly way to stress something: Det er vældig godt (That is very good). It sounds a little old-fashioned.

sentence.da: Maden var **vældig** god.
sentence.en: The food was very good.

værd.explanation: "Værd" means "worth": Den er 100 kroner værd (It is worth 100 kroner). Use it for effort too: Det er værd at prøve (It is worth trying).

forms.en: It is not worth the money.

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel er ikke mange penge **værd**.
sentence.en: The old bike is not worth much money.

værdifuld.explanation: "Værdifuld" means "valuable" and is used for things worth a lot, in money or in meaning: et værdifuldt maleri (a valuable painting). It is built from værdi (value) and fuld (full), so it means "full of value".

sentence.da: Den gamle ring er meget **værdifuld**.
sentence.en: The old ring is very valuable.

værre.explanation: "Værre" means "worse" and is the step up from dårlig (bad). Use it to compare: Det er værre end før (It is worse than before). In et værre rod (quite a mess), it adds emphasis.

sentence.da: I dag er det **værre** end i går.
sentence.en: Today it is worse than yesterday.

værsgo.explanation: "Værsgo" means "here you go" when you hand someone something, and "go ahead" when you invite them to do something: Værsgo, tag en kage (Go ahead, take a cake). The reply is usually tak (thanks). If someone thanks you, say selv tak (you're welcome).

forms.en: Here you go, here is your coffee.

sentence.da: Må jeg låne din pen? **Værsgo**!
sentence.en: May I borrow your pen? Go ahead!

værst.explanation: "Værst" means "worst" and is the step up from værre (worse), which comes from dårlig (bad): Det er værst (It is the worst).

sentence.da: I dag er vejret **værst**.
sentence.en: Today the weather is the worst.
